item.title: Draft Ministerial Ordinance on Color-Coded Inspection Stickers for Small Vessels
item.description: AI summary: The draft Ministerial Ordinance would amend Form No. 15 of the Regulations for Enforcement of the Ship Safety Act (Ministry of Transport Ordinance No. 41 of 1963), under the Ship Safety Act (Act No. 11 of 1933). The vessel-number portion of small-vessel inspection stickers would have a gray background, or green for vessels used in businesses covered by permissions under Articles 3(1), 19-6(1) or 21(1), or registrations under Articles 20(1) or 22(1), of the Maritime Transportation Act (Act No. 187 of 1949), helping users distinguish such vessels. Existing stickers would receive transitional recognition until the first periodic inspection after commencement. The Maritime Bureau, Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism published the proposal for public comment on 2026-11-18, with a stated deadline of 2026-12-17 23:59 JST. The explanatory document schedules promulgation for early January 2027 and commencement for 2027-07-01; these are proposed dates, not confirmation of enactment. item.title: Draft amendments to vertiport guidelines and off-airport takeoff and landing permission procedures
item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism published draft amendments on 2026-11-18 to the Vertiport Development Guidelines, Regional Civil Aviation Bureau procedures for off-airport takeoff and landing permissions, and aviation security service procedures covering flight information services. The proposals would make transitional surfaces optional, revise Protected Side Slope provisions, add a slope-design category for shortened approach surfaces, and clarify conditions for approach-direction intersection angles below 135 degrees or a single approach surface. They would also add guidance on lateral transit and rooftop vertiports, and allow the heads of the Safety Policy Division or Unmanned Aircraft Safety Division, separately or jointly, to establish separate handling arrangements for permission procedures not covered by the aviation security service procedures. The explanatory document states that, pending domestic vertiport standards, flying-car takeoffs and landings are permitted through permissions under the proviso to Article 79 of the Civil Aeronautics Act (Act No. 231 of 1952). The stated comment deadline is 2026-12-18 17:00 JST, and application of the amendments is planned for January 2027. item.title: Draft ministerial ordinance on vocational skills tests for vacuum forming and concrete-block work
item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare published a draft ministerial ordinance on 2026-11-17 to amend the Enforcement Regulations of the Human Resources Development Promotion Act (Ministry of Labour Ordinance No. 24 of 1969), under Articles 44(1) and 51 of the Human Resources Development Promotion Act (Act No. 64 of 1969). The draft would add Grade 3 vacuum-forming test subjects and scope within the plastic-molding occupation, and a basic-grade test for concrete-block construction work within the block-construction occupation. These additions would support skills assessment under the employment-for-skill-development system; the overview describes the related sector-policy changes as subject to further government approval and plans tests from fiscal 2027. The draft also proposes replacing references to technical intern trainees with foreign nationals under the employment-for-skill-development system in Article 66(4), alongside other adjustments associated with Act No. 60 of 2024 amending immigration and technical-intern-training legislation. The stated comment deadline is 2026-12-17 00:00 JST; promulgation is planned for mid-January 2027, with a proposed effective date of 2027-04-01. item.title: Draft Cabinet Order and Cabinet Office Ordinances on sustainability disclosure, assurance and startup funding
item.description: AI summary: On November 13, 2026, the Financial Services Agency published proposed amendments to related Cabinet Orders, Cabinet Office Ordinances and other instruments, including a new assurance-procedure ordinance, to implement provisions of the Act Partially Amending the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act and the Payment Services Act (Act No. 64 of 2026), enacted on July 15, 2026; the relevant statutory provisions take effect on April 1, 2027. The proposals would require companies listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime Market with average market capitalization of at least JPY 500 billion, measured at the preceding five fiscal year-ends, to prepare specified non-financial information under designated standards and obtain assurance from registered providers. They would designate SSBJ standards published by June 11, 2026, and add special procedures for approving extensions of annual securities report filing deadlines. Proposed assurance-provider requirements include minimum capital of JPY 20 million, a quality-control function, engagement personnel with relevant knowledge and at least three years of experience, conflict-of-interest restrictions, and seven-year personnel rotation with a two-year cooling-off period. The proposals also cover assurance reports, disclosure of provider identity and fees, and extraordinary reporting upon a provider change; startup funding is another stated subject, but its detailed provisions are not included in the supplied excerpt.
